subject: Horizon AI — dedicated capacity discovery: recap & immediate asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@horizon.ai>, Procurement <procure@horizon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Horizon AI — dedicated capacity discovery: recap & immediate asks

Samira / team,

Thanks for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick written recap and the immediate asks so we can move toward a proposed committed pool. I kept this focused so procurement and engineering can action items quickly.

Summary of what you said was most important
- Primary workload: low-latency inference (chat + batch embeddings) for product search and conversational support.
- Isolation requirement: dedicated pool with tenant-level data isolation (PHI in some workloads) + audit logs retained 12 months.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~1200 qps equivalent (short prompts, ~40 tokens per request) with 10–15% daily spikes to ~2500 qps; peak traffic windows are US-west business hours.
- SLA targets: production p95 latency < 200 ms; availability goal 99.9% for core endpoints; data residency in us-west.
- Timeline: procurement target = end of Q3; want pilot/canary in mid-August.

Open/next questions (to confirm)
1) Can you share a 48–72 hour representative traffic dump (anonymized) or a token distribution histogram so we can finalize batching/instance mix?
2) For PHI traffic: will that be routed to a separate tenant within the same pool or require an isolated physical pool?
3) Are there any hard procurement constraints (PO terms, insurance minimums, or required contract language) we should know before drafting the commitment?
4) Any preferred runbook/monitoring integrations (Splunk, Datadog, internal tracing) we should add to the ops checklist?

Recommended immediate actions from our side
- I'll circulate a sizing BOM and an ops runbook draft for your team to review (attached: redwood-dedicated-bom.xlsx).
- Ben (cc'd) will draft a short pool-sizing sketch and a canary plan we can run in mid-August.
- If procurement is ready, please share your procurement contact and required legal terms; we can do an initial commercial sketch while engineering finishes sizing.

Attachments: Horizon_Discovery_Summary.pdf (recap deck), redwood-dedicated-bom.xlsx (preliminary BOM)

Thanks — I'll check back after you share the traffic histogram and procurement contact.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee

From: Samira Khan <samira@horizon.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Re: Horizon AI — dedicated capacity discovery: recap & immediate asks

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the succinct recap. A few quick answers while I loop in procurement/security: 

- Traffic: I can export a 72-hour anonymized token histogram and sample qps timeline by EOD Monday. Expect the token distribution to be small-tail heavy (20–60 tokens typical), but we do have occasional long-context requests up to 512 tokens for batch reranking.
- PHI: we'll need strict separation. Ideally a logically isolated tenant in the dedicated pool is fine for us as long as we have separate keys and audit logs; we prefer a separate physical pool only if cost is similar.
- Procurement: Procure@horizon.ai is our procurement lead; they require a standard vendor questionnaire and an expedited PO path for pilots under $25k. Enrollment in your SOC2 evidence sharing would speed security review.
- Timeline: pilot mid-August sounds good; production by end of Q3 is our internal target but can shift one sprint if sizing requires it.

I'll share the histogram and loop in procurement/security on this thread. Thanks for the fast follow-up.

Samira
Director of Platform Engineering | Horizon AI
samira@horizon.ai | +1 (650) 555-0912
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@horizon.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 18:22:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Re: Horizon AI — dedicated capacity discovery: recap & immediate asks

Samira — thanks for the clarity. A couple of technical notes and a proposed next step.

Quick notes based on the profile you gave:
- Baseline/peak sizing: with typical 40-token requests and your baseline/peak qps, our initial recommendation is a committed pool of 6–8 x A100-80GB (or equivalent Ampere 4: 8x) with a small 2x burst reserve to handle 15% spikes. We can convert to cheaper 80-bit quantized instances for non-PHI workloads to lower unit cost.
- Isolation approach: logical tenancy + separate KMS keys + tenant-level network controls should meet the PHI requirement in most cases; if Horizon requires physical separation we can provision a physically isolated pool (adds ~20% overhead).
- Latency & SLA: to hit p95 <200ms we recommend continuous batching with a max batching window of 8ms and tail-latency guard rails; we target 99.9% availability SLA for core endpoints in the committed pool contract.

Concrete next step I'd like to propose:
1) You share the 72-hr traffic sample and any representative prompt set (anonymized).
2) We run a sizing simulation (1–2 business days) and return a short pool-sizing proposal (I'll attach pool-sizing-proposal.pdf to the draft).
3) If the simulation aligns, we propose a 6-week pilot: 2-week canary (10% traffic), 2-week ramp, 2-week stabilization; during the pilot we'll validate batching, cache effectiveness, and ops runbook.

Security/resources: Vivek (cc) can coordinate SOC2 artifact access and the questionnaire. Vivek, could you confirm the SOC2 evidence flow and approximate turnaround for sharing?

Attached: pool-sizing-proposal.pdf (sketch)

Cheers,
--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0203
